title: Bakit Namatay ang Grid-Tied Solar sa Brownout?
audience: Grid-tied solar owners surprised by outages
premise: Grid-tied inverters must stop exporting when the grid is down (anti-islanding) to protect line workers; backup needs a battery and backup setup.

cues.text: Bakit namatay ang solar mo noong nag-brownout?
Kapag nawala ang grid, kusang namamatay ang grid-tied inverter.
Para walang kuryenteng dumaloy pabalik sa linya.
Proteksyon ito sa mga nag-aayos ng linya.
Para may kuryente sa brownout, kailangan ng battery at backup setup.
Dahil ang gusto ni Kuya SoLight… naka-solar ka na, SoSmart ka pa!

sources.title: Net-Metering Rules and Interconnection Standards (Philippine Distribution Code framework)
excerpts: Net-metered systems follow the Philippine Distribution Code and ERC Net-Metering Interconnection Standards, which include islanding protection.

sources.title: Backup power function
excerpts: Backup operation requires a compatible battery and the appropriate backup wiring/switching to separate the home circuits from the grid.

sources.title: Unintentional islanding requirement of IEEE Std 1547-2018 (NREL/TP-5D00-77782)
excerpts: Anti-islanding requires inverters to stop energizing a de-energized grid section; a key reason is personnel (line worker) safety.

sources.title: Guerilla solar installations need to be controlled, says Philippine power distributor
excerpts: In a compliant system, the inverter must immediately disconnect when the grid goes down to prevent backfeeding electricity into power lines.

sources.title: Battery-backup function
excerpts: Battery-backup operation must be set up and wired as a backup system.
